issue.title: Warm project_stats queries take ~2 s: 5 ms git child-exit poll plus ~60 git spawns per project

task_type_fields.impact:
Every `sase stats project` invocation pays ~2.5–4 s, and the Admin Center Statistics →
Projects tab reruns the `{output, runs}` and `{code}` queries on every 30-second tick,
burning ~3.5–4 s of background CPU per tick and showing "refreshing…" for that long.
Warm latency is ~14–20× the approved 150 ms budget. Shared git runner, so other
`file_history` callers pay the same per-spawn sleep.
task_type_fields.location: sase-core crates/sase_core/src/file_history/runner.rs (WAIT_POLL_INTERVAL / run_spawned) and project_stats repo probing; sase src/sase/stats/project/request.py remote lookups
task_type_fields.repro:
Proposed by phase bead sase-1m3.12 (note #1, epic sase-1m3 acceptance), which measured
3,158 ms for a warm `{output, runs}` query and 1,128 ms for a warm `{code}` query on
apollo against the plan's §6.3 budgets (warm, one project: under 150 ms; warm LoC under
0.5 s). Triaged and profiled by the sase-1m3 land agent at sase master 4e5b7d2eb6 /
sase-core f0f2275f (installed release binding), 2026-10-19, host load ~3.

Warm timings (second and later calls, `sase.core.project_stats_facade.query_project_stats`
with the request `load_project_stats` builds for the default 7d preset, 4 enabled
projects):

- `{output, runs}`: ~2,130–2,190 ms; `{output}` alone ~2,110 ms; `{runs}` alone ~530 ms;
  `{code}` ~1,640 ms. `build_project_stats_request` adds another ~280 ms in Python.
- Ablation of `{output}`: one tiny project (tailnet, 4 commits) alone still costs ~480 ms,
  sase alone ~755 ms; dropping the four agents sidecars saves ~290 ms; dropping
  `include_run_only_projects` saves ~550 ms. So the cost is a large fixed per-source
  overhead, not history size.

Root causes found:

1. **Fixed 5 ms child-exit poll.** `crates/sase_core/src/file_history/runner.rs`
   `run_spawned` polls `child.try_wait()` and sleeps `WAIT_POLL_INTERVAL` (5 ms) between
   polls, so every git spawn costs at least one 5 ms sleep even when git exits in ~2 ms.
   `py-spy record --native --idle` over four warm queries shows ~48% of all samples in
   `clock_nanosleep` called directly from `sase_core_rs` inside `query_project_stats`.
2. **Too many git spawns per warm query.** `strace -f -e execve` of one warm one-project
   (tailnet) query shows ~60 successful `git` spawns: per repo/sidecar separate
   `rev-parse --show-toplevel`, `--git-common-dir`, `--git-path …`,
   `--is-shallow-repository`, several `rev-parse --verify`, and
   `rev-list --max-parents=0`, repeated for the project's code repo, plans/beads/research
   sidecars, attachments sidecars, and every project's agents sidecar (the agents
   sidecar list is not narrowed to the selected projects). The Python request builder
   separately spawns `git config --get remote.origin.url` / `git remote -v` /
   `git remote get-url origin` ~28 times.

Repro (from a sase checkout with its venv):

```python
import time
from datetime import UTC, datetime
from sase.stats.project.query import ProjectStatsQuery
from sase.stats.project.request import build_project_stats_request
from sase.core.project_stats_facade import query_project_stats
from sase.stats.ranges import resolve_preset
q = ProjectStatsQuery(range=resolve_preset("7d"), preset="7d")
req = build_project_stats_request(q, facets=frozenset({"output", "runs"}),
                                  now_ts=int(datetime.now(UTC).timestamp()))
query_project_stats(req.data)  # cold/warm-up
t0 = time.perf_counter(); query_project_stats(req.data)
print(f"warm {(time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1000:.0f} ms")
```

Suggested direction: adaptive child-exit waiting (sub-millisecond first polls with
backoff, or wait on stdout EOF before polling), one batched `rev-parse` per repository
for identity/common-dir/shallow/ref probes, a per-process memo of repo identity keyed on
cheap stat tokens, and narrowing agents sidecars to the selected projects; likewise
batch or memoize the Python-side remote-URL lookups. Re-measure against the §6.3
budgets of plan:202610/sase_stats_project.md.

issue.creation_reason: Phase sase-1m3.12 recorded a >2x warm-latency budget miss as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP; the sase-1m3 land agent profiled it and found two concrete root causes, which the approved plan routes to a follow-up rather than blocking the epic.

payload.description: Shared fixed per-spawn git overhead inflates the Code cold/changed-tip numbers; fix or re-measure together
Same file_history git runner; a batching or child-wait redesign may collide with the non-deadlocking batch migration
